headline: Huang's return sparks a short squeeze: Nvidia +31%, SOX +14%; Taiwan futures limit-up overnight
summary: Last night's US rally was a news-driven short squeeze, not a trend change: the S&P 500 is still below its 200-day line, so by the rules it remains a pullback. Taiwan will likely gap up today with a TSMC ADR premium of 18%, but foreign investors have sold for 6 straight days; watch whether they buy back today. Keep regular investing on plan.

watch.note: 11/23 close 7,237.17, 1.5% away; 5 straight closes below. Reclaiming it would repair the trend.

watch.label: TAIEX -20% line
watch.note: 11/23 close 36,811.89, 8.3% away; night futures hit limit-up at 40,324. First check: can the open hold above it.

overview.lead: Last night was a news-driven short squeeze: Nvidia's board reinstated Jensen Huang, and chips won back most of last week's losses in a day. The broad trend is not repaired yet.
points: The S&P 500 rose 4.73% and the Nasdaq 6.51%, the biggest one-day gains in about a year and a half.
The SOX rose 14.03% to 9,588.
Nvidia (NVDA) rose 31.48%, its best day since 2003.
Gains were concentrated in chips: the equal-weight S&P 500 (RSP) rose only 2.6%, while energy and staples slipped.
The S&P 500 is still 1.5% below its 200-day line; by the rules it remains a pullback.

focus.lead: Among the nine tracked names, US and tech bounced most: QQQ rose 7% and moved away from tier 4. But three fund NAVs only run to 11/20 and miss last night's rally.
points: QQQ rose 7.0% and SPY 4.7%; 0050 will reflect it at today's Taiwan open.
AB International Technology (LU0060230025) and AB Select US Equity (LU0683600562) NAVs run only to 11/20; top holding Nvidia rose 31% last night.
The two AB funds share 7 top-ten names, about 24% by weight, Nvidia included, so their moves amplify each other.
AB Select US Equity's 11/20 NAV reached tier 2; tier 3 is 4.8% away.
Allianz Taiwan Technology (TW000T3604Y3) and Cathay Taiwan High Dividend (TW000T3786A8) 11/23 NAVs are still -42% and -37% from highs.
Neuberger Berman Taiwan-Japan (TW000T5011A9) NAV stops at 11/20 and misses Taiwan's 11/23 bounce.

position.lead: Under the framework, last night's rally triggered nothing new; it widened every gap to the next tier. 0050's tier 5 will likely move further away today.
points: QQQ has used 45% of reserved cash; tier 4 is 6.7% away.
SPY has used 25% of reserved cash; tier 3 is 8.3% away.
0050 has used 70% of reserved cash; tier 5 is 6.3% away.
AB Select US Equity's 11/20 NAV reached tier 2, using 25% of reserved cash.
Fidelity Japan Value (LU0997587083) is 10.5% from tier 5; Neuberger Berman Taiwan-Japan is 6.7% away.
Allianz Taiwan Technology, Cathay Taiwan High Dividend and AB International Technology have used all tiers.

macro.lead: The rally had nothing to do with macro, and rates still lean tight: markets still price a December hike, and the 10-year yield did not jump with stocks.
points: The 10-year Treasury yield is 4.92%; the 10-year minus 3-month spread is 0.55 points, not inverted.
Polymarket shows about 91% odds of a hike at the 12/9 meeting.
The high-yield spread is 3.76% (11/20), up 0.49 points in a month, still short of the warning line.
USD/TWD is 32.97 (11/20), a weak level for the Taiwan dollar by ten-year standards.
PCE inflation and Q3 GDP on 11/25 are the next test for hike expectations.

sentiment.lead: One big day has not washed out the fear: the Fear & Greed index is still at extreme fear, and the volatility curve is still inverted.
points: The VIX fell to 26.62, still above its long-run median of 17.6.
The Fear & Greed index is 17; a week ago it was 31.
The 9-day VIX at 27.76 is above the 3-month at 25.5; short-term hedging demand has not faded.
A Nomura strategist called it a short-covering "mechanical bounce" that guarantees nothing.
Only 5 of 11 sectors are above their 200-day lines.

sectors.lead: Last week's biggest losers bounced most: chips and memory led, defensives stood still. A classic oversold squeeze.
points: Semiconductors (SMH) rose 15.0% but are still down 12.7% over a month.
Micron (MU) rose 19.04%; the SK Hynix ADR rose about 20%.
Tech (XLK) rose 9.0%; software (IGV) only 3.9%.
Energy (XLE) fell 1.1% and staples (XLP) 0.1%; money rotated from defense back to tech.
Microsoft (MSFT) rose only 1.65% and Apple (AAPL) 1.9%, the smallest gains among megacaps.

taiwan.lead: Taiwan will likely gap up sharply today, and night futures already priced it: TAIEX futures hit limit-up and TSMC futures rose nearly 10%.
points: The TSMC ADR rose 14.08% to US$363.60.
The ADR premium is 18.3%; even limit-up, TSMC (2330) spot can only reach about NT$2,233 today.
TAIEX night futures rose as much as 3,665 points to 40,324, hitting limit-up.
TSMC futures closed the night session at NT$2,238, up 9.98%.
Foreign investors have sold for 6 straight days, NT$247.6B in total; whether they buy today decides if the bounce lasts.
The margin maintenance ratio drops from 130% to 120% from today, easing forced-selling pressure.

watch.lead: First, see whether Taiwan holds its gap today; then Dell earnings tonight and PCE tomorrow night. For the bounce to last, fundamentals must take over from the news.
points: TAIEX -20% line at 39,858: night futures are above it; holding it at the spot close is the first test.
Foreign net buying today would be the first sign the selling is stopping.
S&P 500 200-day line at 7,350, 1.5% away.
Dell (DELL) earnings on 11/24 test AI server demand.
US PCE inflation and Q3 GDP on 11/25; US markets close 11/26 for Thanksgiving.

regime.lead: By the rules, the US is still a "pullback" and Taiwan still a "bear market, risk rising"; one big day changes neither call.
points: Trend: the S&P 500 is 1.5% below its 200-day line with 5 straight closes below, but the line is still rising.
Systemic lights: only "US market below the 200-day line" is on; credit, the economy and financial conditions show no problem yet.
Closest to turning on is credit: the high-yield spread rose 0.49 points in a month, against a 0.75 trigger.
Panic-bottom signals: the US has two on, an inverted volatility curve and extreme fear.
History: of 133 S&P 500 declines that reached this level, 19 went past -20%; most stopped near -10%.
Of the 51 that were this fast and still above the 200-day line, only 5 went past -20%.
What would flip the call: 5 S&P 500 closes below 7,350 with a flat 200-day line means weak.
Taiwan must close back above 39,858, then hold its 200-day line for 5 days, to return to a correction.
Nasdaq 100 regime data runs only to 11/19 and does not include last night's rally.
